fields.statement: How is an arbiter ruling applied when the finding's node lives in a serving draft change set and the arbiter's Decision lives in the run's intention change set? Neither change set's view holds both nodes, so rhiza apply refuses the decided-by link in either (not_found, by handle and by ID), and review-check --rulings can never pass for such a ruling. plan-workflow-autonomous-left.txtar hits exactly this: finding f1 is on leaf export-csv in the serving draft, its question and the arbiter's Decision settle-... land in the intention change set; f2 on landed keep-flat applies fine. In real autonomous plan runs leaves live in serving drafts, so every leaf ruling would end the run failed. Options: (a) the arbiter writes its Decision in the change set holding the finding's node; (b) review-check leaves the question there; (c) --rulings accepts another witness; (d) narrow this leaf's script to rulings on nodes the run's change set sees. The workflow steps (plan.toml, plan-milestone.toml), the unit test and the five 'then rulings' script assertions are built and pass in the working tree, uncommitted.
